title: Multi‑Host Multi‑Port Scanner (Nested Loops)
description: Use nested loops to scan several hosts on several ports and report the results.
problemStatement:
Write a script `multi_scanner.py` that defines two lists: `hosts = ["192.168.1.1", "10.0.0.2"]` and `ports = [22, 80, 443]`. Use nested `for` loops to iterate over each host and each port. For each combination, print "Scanning [host] on port [port]...". Inside the inner loop, after printing, check if the port is 80 and the host is "10.0.0.2" – if so, print "-> Web server found on unexpected host!" and use `break` to stop scanning further ports for that host (but continue with next hosts).

Note: `break` inside the inner loop only exits that inner loop; outer loop continues.

Expected output should show all scans for first host, and for second host stop after port 80.
hints: After printing, if condition matches, print special message and break.
You can use a for‑else to print a summary per host, but not required.
expectedOutput:
Scanning 192.168.1.1 on port 22...
Scanning 192.168.1.1 on port 80...
Scanning 192.168.1.1 on port 443...
Scanning 10.0.0.2 on port 22...
Scanning 10.0.0.2 on port 80...
-> Web server found on unexpected host!
